sentences.text:
The appellant-Insurance Company is before this Court aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.07.2017 passed in MVC No.185/2015 by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Shorapur,
('Tribunal'), by NC: 2023:KHC-K:8626 which, the Tribunal relying upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun V/s.

Divisional manager, National Ins., Co. Ltd., and Anr.,
reported in 2013 AIAR (Civil) Page 959 Supreme Court of India, has awarded compensation of Rs.3,45,000/- to the injured-claimant.

2 2.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that the only grievance of the appellant- Insurance Company is that the injured-claimant admittedly suffered disability of 10% and as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Master Mallikarjun's case referred supra compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is to be payable to the disability up to 10% and Rs.3,00,000/- is to be payable only for cases where the disability is above 20% and up to 30%.
Thus, he submits that, in the instant case since the disability is assessed at 10% compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- ought to have been awarded and not Rs.3,00,000/-.

Further, he submits that once the compensation is awarded in terms of the judgment in NC: 2023:KHC-K:8626 Master Mallikarjun's case, there is no question of awarding any compensation under any other heads, whereas, in the instant case Tribunal ought not to have awarded additional sum of Rs.40,000/-.
On these counts the appellant-Insurance Company is aggrieved.

3. Sri Chaitanyakumar C.M., learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1-claimant on the other hand submits that in the judgment of Apex Court in Master Marllikarjun's, case the language used is 'below 10% and above 10%'.
Therefore, he submits wherever the disability is assessed at 10% it has to be construed falling above 10% entitling the claimant to claim of Rs.3,00,000/-.
As regards award of additional compensation he submits that the Tribunal is justified in awarding the same considering the age of the minor child, therefore, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8626 5.

The Tribunal while relying upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun has relied upon at Para 12 of the judgment, which reads as under:
"Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%,
Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.
Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents."
Perusal of the above would reveal that compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- is payable if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body.
Admittedly, in the instant case, respondent No.1 has suffered disability of 10%.
The Tribunal therefore awarded compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.

The same cannot be found fault with and no interpretation needs to be given with regard to the terms The Divisional Manager, National vs Rahul S/O Y Sharanappa on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130470221/
3 'above and below 10%'.

sentences.text: 7. However, there is justifiable grounds to interfere with the award of additional compensation of Rs.45,000/- towards pain and suffering as the said Rs.3,00,000/- include even the compensation towards pain and suffering.
To the said extent the award of the Tribunal is modified reducing the compensation payable to the injured-claimant-respondent to the extent of at Rs.3,00,000/- and not Rs.3,45,000/-.
The appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award by the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
9. The claimant-respondent is entitled for Rs.3,00,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
10. The amount in deposit, if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal.
